back: The fraction of incoming shortwave radiation a surface reflects (reflected ÷ incoming). Earth's average is about 0.3; fresh snow about 0.8-0.9; forest about 0.1.
The Sun emits shortwave radiation; the cooler Earth emits longwave (infrared) radiation, which greenhouse gases absorb.
Longwave radiation emitted downwards by the atmosphere (greenhouse gases and cloud), warming the surface.
Energy taken up when water evaporates and released when the vapour condenses; moves energy upwards in the atmosphere.

front: Natural greenhouse effect: how much warming?
back: About 33 °C: average surface temperature about +15 °C instead of about −18 °C without greenhouse gases.
Clear skies let longwave radiation escape to space, with little back radiation, so the ground cools quickly; cloud slows cooling.
About 30 reflected or scattered (26 by cloud and atmosphere, 4 by the surface), about 20 absorbed by the atmosphere, about 50 absorbed by the surface.
The difference between the highest and lowest temperatures in a 24-hour period; larger under clear, dry skies.
